title: Research Taste Exercises
focus_en: Proposes exercises for developing research taste through cheap, noisy feedback from mentors, making repeated judgments more practical than waiting for the expensive feedback of fully executed research.
focus_zh: 提出利用导师提供的低成本、带噪声反馈练习 research taste，让研究者能够反复训练判断，而不必每次等待完整研究执行后的高成本反馈。
boundary_en: The author presents a rough note rather than a validated training program; mentor ratings are proxies for research quality, and the exercises have not demonstrated improvements in AI research taste.
boundary_zh: 作者将其定位为粗略笔记，未验证训练方案的有效性；导师评分只是研究质量的代理，也没有证据表明这些练习能提升 AI 的 research taste。

title: A Survival Guide to a PhD
focus_en: Connects research taste with choosing promising problems, developing ideas, and executing them effectively, offering practical guidance on how computer science and machine learning researchers build research ability.
focus_zh: 将 research taste 与选择有前景的问题、发展想法和有效执行联系起来，为计算机科学与机器学习研究者积累科研能力提供实践建议。
boundary_en: This is first-person advice from a computer science PhD experience, not a controlled study; its recommendations do not establish which interventions reliably improve human or AI research performance.
boundary_zh: 这是基于个人计算机科学博士经历的建议，并非受控研究；它不能确认哪些干预能可靠地提升人类或 AI 的科研表现。

title: You and Your Research
venue: Bellcore lecture; J. F. Kaiser transcript
focus_en: Argues for deliberately choosing important, tractable problems and cultivating the habits, preparation, and working relationships that help researchers recognize opportunities and pursue work with substantial scientific consequences.
focus_zh: 强调主动选择重要且可推进的问题，并培养工作习惯、知识准备与协作关系，使研究者能够识别机会、追求具有重要科学影响的工作。
boundary_en: This Bellcore lecture is preserved in a transcript by J. F. Kaiser mirrored at UVA; its autobiographical observations are not controlled evidence or demonstrated methods for training AI scientists.
boundary_zh: 收录版本为 UVA 镜像的 J. F. Kaiser 整理的 Bellcore 演讲稿；其中的个人经历与观察不是受控证据，也不是经过验证的 AI 科学家训练方法。

title: Research Debt
focus_en: Frames accumulated complexity and poor communication as research debt, arguing that distillation, better abstractions, and clear explanations are productive research contributions that enable others to understand and extend existing knowledge.
focus_zh: 将积累的复杂性与沟通障碍概括为 research debt，强调知识提炼、改进抽象和清晰解释也是科研贡献，能够帮助他人理解与拓展已有知识。
boundary_en: This conceptual editorial motivates improving cumulative research infrastructure; it does not provide a validated benchmark, causal estimate of distillation's benefits, or evidence that an AI system can perform these contributions.
boundary_zh: 这篇概念性文章倡议改善知识积累的基础条件，但未提供经过验证的 benchmark、知识提炼收益的因果估计，或 AI 能完成这些贡献的证据。

title: Quick thoughts on research
focus_en: Offers heuristics for discovering worthwhile problems, developing judgment through tacit knowledge, and learning from research postmortems, treating research ability as something cultivated through reflection on concrete experience.
focus_zh: 围绕发现值得研究的问题、从隐性知识中发展判断力，以及通过 research postmortems 学习提出启发式建议，将科研能力视为对具体经验持续反思的结果。
boundary_en: These are individual research heuristics with limits acknowledged by the author, not a systematic evaluation; translating them into measurable training objectives or reliable AI learning mechanisms remains an open task.
boundary_zh: 这些是作者明确承认局限的个人科研经验，并非系统评价；如何将其转化为可测量的训练目标或可靠的 AI 学习机制仍是开放问题。

title: A Vision of Metascience: An Engine of Improvement for the Social Processes of Science
focus_en: Proposes metascience as a way to improve science's social processes, including resource allocation and institutional design, by building institutions that learn how to support better research.
focus_zh: 提出以 metascience 改进科学活动的社会过程，包括资源分配与制度设计，并建立能够持续学习如何更好支持科研的机构。
boundary_en: This is a conceptual agenda for institutional improvement rather than an empirical AI method; better social processes and stronger individual research agents require distinct mechanisms and evidence.
boundary_zh: 这是改进科研制度的概念性议程，而非实证 AI 方法；改善社会过程与增强个体 research agent 需要不同的机制与证据。
